text:
maya: paging: we're seeing a spike in KV prefix error rate and correctness regressions affecting v2 inference pools. alerting shows 8xx/5xx from serving runtime + mismatched outputs. paging rahul oncall.
oncall-bot: @rahul you are on-call for incidents (rotation start 2109120000). Incident created: INCIDENT-2109.
rahul: I'm on it. first glance: internal dashboards show prefix-hit ratio dropped for tenant:acme by 60% and a concurrent surge in cold reads to backing store. tail latency up ~450ms p50->p99.
dave: seeing a lot of KV cache evictions around prefix hash 0x7f9a, suspect rapid churn from a hotkey pattern + background prefetch thrash.
jess: @rahul any customer-facing errors or retries? CS says one large customer reported hallucinations — might be related to stale prefixes.
customer-success: acme reports inconsistent completions; some queries returning older cached responses intermittently. they're on slack, asking for mitigation.
eng-runtime: logs show a misapplied eviction policy after a recent rollout of degen-config v2 that aggressively prioritizes memory compaction. could be interacting poorly with prefix pinning.
rahul: ok mitigation plan: 1) isolate affected prefix keyspace; 2) temporarily set prefix-cache-bypass for tenant:acme to true; 3) apply emergency rate balancing to reduce background prefetch; 4) pause degen-config rollout on runtime.
maya: agree. prioritize correctness over cost; we can accept higher token spend for acme while we stabilize.
ops-bot: Running change: POST /admin/tenants/acme/cache_override { "bypass_prefix_cache": true }
ops-bot: Change succeeded on node-set: us-west-1a (3/3).
rahul: rolling traffic shaping: set request-level concurrency cap to 20 for tenant:acme and throttle prefetch worker group to 10% capacity.
eng-runtime: applying rate-limit rule: 
```
# gateway rate limit override
route: /v1/generate
tenant: acme
limit: 20rps
burst: 5
```
eng-runtime: rule applied via config push to edge-proxy cluster.
dave: also bumping eviction threshold to keep prefetched keys for 30s longer on affected hosts to reduce backing store pressure.
jess: customer message drafted: "We're investigating a caching issue causing inconsistent outputs. We have temporarily disabled prefix caching for your traffic and applied throttles to avoid further instability. We expect reduced latency variance within the hour." Want me to send now?
customer-success: please send, include that we're prioritizing correctness and will provide updates every 30m.
rahul: monitoring: adding synthetic checks hitting hot prefixes, and bolting on additional tracing for prefix version ids.
eng-runtime: tracing shows some requests still hitting stale entries due to race in prefix invalidation path; bypass flag should prevent reads, but a few in-flight requests may still return older values.
emily: suggest also incrementally raising token quota limits for acme while bypass increases backend cost so we don't hit quota errors for their heavy flows.
maya: yes, set temporary quota window: tokens-per-minute -> +50% for acme for 2 hours. ops-bot: Running quota change: POST /admin/tenants/acme/quota {"tpm": "+50%", "duration": "120m"}
ops-bot: Quota update accepted.
rahul: OK next steps: 1) monitor correctness metrics for 30m; 2) if stable, re-enable prefix reads for a narrow subset (canary) of prefixes with strict version check; 3) rollback degen-config rollout. Who can rollback?
eng-runtime: I can push rollback for degen-config across runtime nodes, will coordinate with eng-sre.
dave: coordinating handoff to night on-call @jess in 40m. I'll leave runbook notes: cause = aggressive compaction + hotkey churn, mitigation = bypass + rate shaping + eviction threshold relax, customer comms sent.
jess: taking oncall in 40m, will continue monitoring. please post runbook snippet in incident doc.
maya: please also capture exact config diffs for audit (push ids). rahul and eng-runtime, attach config hashes to the incident ticket.
rahul: noted. pushing tracing snapshots and config hashes to INCIDENT-2109.
eng-runtime: initial observations: bypass increases backend QPS by ~3x for those prefixes but error rate drops to baseline and output divergence stops.
customer-success: acme confirms behaviour improved after bypass; inconsistencies reduced, some latency increase but acceptable. they asked about long term fix.
maya: long term action items: 1) revert degen-config or tune compaction thresholds; 2) implement prefix invalidation safeties (idempotent invalidation); 3) add per-tenant surge shielding to avoid hotkey churn hitting the prefix index; 4) improve prefetch backoff heuristics. Assign owners in ticket.
ops-bot: Incident status -> mitigation in place, customer impact reduced. Next update scheduled in 30 minutes.
rahul: handoff to jess when she goes oncall. jess: ack, will take it.
maya: thanks team. closing live channel for now, we will keep incident ticket open and post a short postmortem after root cause confirmed. :thumbsup:
